gitCommit.subject: fix(canvas): add loading indicator overlay during inpainting (#1471)
gitCommit.body:
fix(canvas): add loading indicator overlay during inpainting (#1471)

* fix(canvas): persist imageIds on inpaint completion

onGenerationComplete was not destructuring imageIds from the generation
result, so canvas save serialized stale imageIds. After page reload or
publish, the old image was displayed instead of the inpainted result.

Extract buildInpaintedImageUpdate for testability and include imageIds
and imageId in the onUpdateImage call.

* fix(canvas): add loading indicator overlay during inpainting

Show a semi-transparent overlay with spinner on the target image while
inpainting is in progress. The indicator persists even when the image
is deselected and auto-clears when generation completes or fails.

- Add inpaintingObjectId field to paint-state store
- Create InpaintLoadingIndicator Konva component (listening=false)
- Wire up setInpaintingObjectId in use-canvas-inpainting hook
- Mount indicator in gazai-canvas Layer stack

* fix(canvas): address PR review findings for inpaint loading indicator

Move inpainting cleanup (setIsInpaintGenerating, setInpaintingObjectId)
to a finally block to prevent stuck overlay when generateOnCanvas returns
early (e.g. insufficient tokens). Conditionally render the indicator
Layer to avoid empty Konva layer overhead. Fix non-Error Sentry
reporting and replace console.warn with structured logger.

* fix(canvas): add listening={false} to inpaint indicator Layer

Konva Layers create independent canvas elements that intercept pointer
events even when all child nodes have listening={false}. Setting
listening={false} on the Layer itself ensures the entire canvas is
skipped during hit testing, allowing drag events to pass through to
the image objects on layers below.

Closes TSK-4451

* fix(canvas): render inpaint overlay inside ImageNode for drag-follow

Move InpaintOverlay from a separate Layer into ImageNode's Group so
it automatically follows the image during drag. Also prevent
GenerationLoadingIndicator from rendering during inpainting.

* fix(canvas): drag-to-move image via inpainting gazai-chan indicator

During inpainting, users expect to drag the gazai-chan loading
indicator to reposition the image being processed. Two bugs prevented
this from working:

1. Indicator position was locked to `generation.indicatorPosition`
   (set once at generation start) because the `{x,y}` useMemo had no
   `referenceImage` dependency. The indicator stayed put while the
   image moved, so drag base never updated and subsequent drags
   calculated huge incorrect deltas.

2. `stage.findOne('#id')` could return the KonvaImage inside the
   ImageNode Group instead of the Group itself (both share the same
   id). Moving the Image only moved the pixels, leaving the Group
   and InpaintOverlay behind.

Changes:
- Compute `inpaintCenter` from `referenceImage.position` — tracks
  current image center and re-calculates each render.
- After `findOne('#id')`, check className and traverse to parent if
  not a Group — ensures we manipulate the Group (which owns
  position/transform and contains InpaintOverlay).
- Add dark overlay during inpainting (`listening={false}`) for
  consistent visual feedback without blocking pointer events.
- Switch InpaintOverlay spinner from `useState` + rAF to
  `Konva.Animation` — avoids React re-renders that would reset the
  parent Group's dragged position.

* fix(canvas): preserve drag position after inpainting completes

When users dragged the image via the inpainting gazai-chan indicator
during generation, the new position was lost once generation completed
and the image jumped back to its original location.

Root cause: `useCanvasInpainting` captured the `image` prop at
`handleGenerate` invocation. When `onGenerationComplete` fired, it
spread the STALE captured image — `{...image, src: newSrc, ...}` —
overwriting the current store position with the original one.

Fix: Read the current image from `useCanvasStore.getState()` inside
`onGenerationComplete`. This picks up any position, scale, or other
property changes the user made during generation. Falls back to the
captured `image` if the object was removed from the store (edge case).

* fix(canvas): move all matching Groups when image is rendered twice

Some images on the canvas are rendered in multiple places — once as
standalone under the Layer, and once as a panel/frame child inside
another Group. Both share the same id.

The inpainting drag's `stage.findOne('#id')` only returned the first
match (the panel child, which wasn't visually on top). Moving it
caused no visible change, since the standalone Group on top stayed
in place.

Additional bugs fixed in this change:
- Used `getClassName()` method instead of `.className` property.
  Konva's `className` is NOT an instance property; `node.className`
  is undefined on instances, causing the Group-vs-Image check to
  always traverse up (even when we'd already found the Group).
- Used `.getParent()` instead of `.parent` for API consistency.
- Added `draw()` / `batchDraw()` on the affected layers to force
  immediate visual update — Konva setters don't auto-redraw.

`stage.find()` now returns ALL matching nodes; we promote each match
to its containing Group, deduplicate, and move every Group
simultaneously. Layers that host any of the moved Groups are redrawn
as a set.

* fix(canvas): move inpaint overlay in sync with image during drag

The dark overlay in the indicator Layer was positioned from the
store-based `overlayX/overlayY` (derived from `referenceImage.position`).
Since the store isn't updated during drag, the overlay stayed at the
original position while the image moved.

Attach a ref to the overlay Group and move it directly alongside the
image Groups on each drag tick, then batchDraw its layer. The dragEnd
store commit still snaps everything back into sync via React rerender.

* fix(canvas): extract imageIds from inpaint result and guard drag on missing nodes

- Extract imageIds from inpaintResult.outputImages in the
  executeRequestWithRetries lambda so canvas save persists the correct
  image IDs. Previously imageIds was either undefined or referenced a
  non-existent variable, causing a ReferenceError and preventing
  inpainted images from surviving a page refresh.

- Add early return in the inpainting drag handler when stage.find()
  finds no matching Konva nodes, preventing the confusing scenario
  where the mascot indicator moves but the underlying image stays
  frozen in place.

* fix(canvas): use block body in useEffect cleanup to satisfy TS return type

anim.stop() returns a Konva.Animation instance (for method chaining),
but useEffect cleanup must return void. Wrapping in a block body
discards the return value and fixes the TS2345 build error.

* chore: add harness to gitignore
